# Stage-1 kernels on H1: mappings, MFU factors and checks

<!-- generated by `python -m workload_modeling.kernel_explorer`; do not edit by hand -->

Companion to [smolvla-op-graph.md](smolvla-op-graph.md) and [smolvla-op-graph-w1b.md](smolvla-op-graph-w1b.md). For every kernel shape of the composed call it shows the mapping space the drivers in `infra/kernel-runs/` could choose from, what was swept, what was selected, and where the selected kernel loses MFU. The interactive version (mesh diagrams, candidate scatter, Perfetto links) is `infra/workload-modeling/build/kernel-explorer.html`; serve it with `python3 infra/kernel-runs/serve_traces.py`. Two independent plans per lowering (upstream rule, plan-constrained sweep), each with its own runs and picks: where their mapping strategies live in the code is under [How each plan maps its kernels](#how-each-plan-maps-its-kernels-code).

Labels: kernel times, sweep rows and trace events are *measured*; the valid space counts come from the drivers' candidate generators (*inference*); MFU factors, the time budget and busy fractions are *estimate*; composed call and stage times are sums of measured kernel times (*estimate*: no overlap).

**Checks:** 264 of 264 pass (list in [the appendix](#appendix-checks)).

## How each plan maps its kernels (code)

Every number on this page comes from one of two independent kernel-mapping strategies on the same deployment plan. Each plan runs and picks from its own candidates; the two share no runs and no check compares their times (a plan may be better or worse than another). A further spatial-mapping strategy is one more plan: its own driver, its own `constants.yaml` group, its own bundle.

```
deploy_plan.Plan (placement, reshapes, padding) --+--> plan_runs.py  (upstream rule) --+
                                                  |                                    +--> to_constants.py --> constants.yaml
                                                  +--> plan_sweep.py (constrained)  --+        groups --> kernel_set --> this page
```

| part | what it decides | code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| deployment plan (both plans) | HBM placement of every array (space A west, space B south), head-major reshapes, head padding from the attention setting | [`deploy_plan.py`](../../infra/workload-modeling/workload_modeling/deploy_plan.py) `Plan`; lowering [`smolvla_ops.py`](../../infra/workload-modeling/workload_modeling/smolvla_ops.py) `PLAN_LOWERING`, `PLAN_LOWERING_W1B` |
| upstream rule (`h1_plan`, `h1_plan_w1b`) | GEMM: upstream `opt()` candidates fitted to the plan shape (`fit`), plus a fallback if all fail; attention: the `attn_auto` setting the plan carries, recorded fixes; row kernels at default; per key the fastest run that passes the output check | [`plan_runs.py`](../../infra/kernel-runs/plan_runs.py) (`gemm_cands`, `fit`, `fallback`, `other_cands`); [`gemm_upstream.py`](../../infra/kernel-runs/gemm_upstream.py) `opt`; [`upstream_rules.py`](../../infra/workload-modeling/workload_modeling/upstream_rules.py) `attn_opt` |
| plan-constrained sweep (`h1_psweep`, `h1_psweep_w1b`) | same deployment plan; attention-padding combinations for the whole graph (`combos`, `PAD_SLACK`, `PAD_KEEP`), per run variant GEMM top-N by the cost model plus upstream's `opt()` and the earlier pick, attention top-N of the valid space plus the plan setting, Eltwise default and pipeline; runs only its own candidates (independent of the upstream-rule runs; `--with-upstream-runs` opts out); picks the combination with the smallest call total | [`plan_sweep.py`](../../infra/kernel-runs/plan_sweep.py) (`combos`, `gemm_cands`, `attn_cands`, `row_cands`, `pick`) |
| into the composed call | picks -> `constants.yaml` groups; a lowering x selection gives the kernel set | [`to_constants.py`](../../infra/kernel-runs/to_constants.py) `plan_block`; [`smolvla_ops.py`](../../infra/workload-modeling/workload_modeling/smolvla_ops.py) `PLAN_GROUPS`, `kernel_set` |

## Glossary

| term | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| W1 | one policy call of `vlabench-3cam` with its 3 cameras encoded one by one (3 passes through the vision encoder); deployed under the upstream deployment plan. The stage-1 baseline. |
| W1-b | the same call with the 3 cameras batched into one vision pass, under the same upstream deployment plan (q/k/v and gate/up separate products, as on W1); vision attention runs as one call over cameras x heads (36 heads). Differs from W1 in camera batching only. |
| upstream deployment plan (`h1_plan`) | upstream soft_hier_je's whole-graph HBM layout and kernel-selection rule applied to SmolVLA: activations in space A (west HBM edge), weights, residual stream and K/V in space B (south edge); attention operands head-major; GEMM settings from upstream's `opt()`, attention from `attn_auto`, row kernels at default parameters; the fastest run that passes the output check is kept. Times: `constants.yaml h1_plan` (W1), `h1_plan_w1b` (W1-b); runs `results/plan_runs_h1.csv`. |
| plan-constrained sweep (`h1_psweep`) | the same deployment plan (placement, head-major reshapes, head padding carried by every kernel that touches a head-major tensor), with the free knobs searched instead of upstream's rule: attention settings and with them the head padding, chosen for the whole graph (expert self and cross attention share Q, the prefix K/V feed the expert's cross projections); GEMM tile, group shape and strategy fitted to the plan; Eltwise schedule. Runs and picks from its own candidates only (upstream's settings among its seeds, run by the sweep itself); independent of the upstream-rule plan. Times: `constants.yaml h1_psweep` (W1), `h1_psweep_w1b` (W1-b); runs `results/plan_sweep_h1.csv`. |
| × vs left / right | explorer pane header: this plan's call total / the other shown plan's. Plans are independent (own run keys, own mapping strategy); only call totals are set side by side, no per-key ratio. |
| run key | `<stage>.<kernel>_<shape>[_zto|_xfrom][_p<placement>]`: one plan run per key, e.g. `vision.gemm_1024x768x768_zto`. Shape is M x N x K for GEMM, heads x q rows x kv rows x d for attention, rows x columns for row kernels. |
| GEMM setting name | `<technique>_x<X>y<Y>g<G>_t<M>x<N>x<K>` (plan runs): G groups of X x Y clusters, tile M x N x K. The sweeps write square groups as `s<S>` (= `x<S>y<S>`), e.g. `Nosplit_s8g1` = `Nosplit_x8y8g1`. |
| Nosplit / splitN / splitK | SUMMA GEMM on cluster groups. Nosplit: one group computes the whole product. splitN: each of the G groups owns N / G output columns. splitK: each group owns a block of K; the partial sums are added by a NoC reduction. |
| attention setting name | `attn_s<sx>x<sy>_b<Br>x<Bc>`: FlatAttention with one group of sx x sy clusters per KV head (groups take the KV heads in turn), row block Br, column block Bc. |
| `_zto` (RESHA_Z_TO) | the GEMM writes its output Z reshaped (SummaGEMM option GEMM_RESHA_Z_TO, TALL); with the chunk = head dim 64 this stores q/k/v head-major for FlatAttention. |
| `_xfrom` (RESHA_X_FROM) | the GEMM reads its input X from a reshaped (head-major) layout: o_proj reads the attention output, and the expert's cross K/V projections read the prefix K/V. |
| TALL / THIN | the two reshape directions (gemm_config.py): TALL (target rows > M) cuts the columns into chunks and stacks them vertically; THIN (target rows < M) puts row blocks side by side. |
| head-major | (heads, rows per head, d = 64): the layout FlatAttention reads and writes. Rows per head are padded to the attention row tile, which is why plan GEMM shapes can be larger than the logical ones (work ratio). |
| `_p<placement>` suffix | HBM placement that differs from the kernel's default: each pair is an array initial and an edge initial (w = west, s = south). Used here: `_pBwIsOs` (Activation: B_addr south -> west, I_addr west -> south, O_eaddr west -> south); `_pIsOs` (Activation: I_addr west -> south, O_eaddr west -> south); `_pIsOs` (Eltwise: I_addr west -> south, O_eaddr west -> south); `_pIsOsZw` (Eltwise: I_addr west -> south, O_eaddr west -> south, Z_addr south -> west); `_pOs` (Eltwise: O_eaddr west -> south); `_pXs` (SummaGEMM: X_addr west -> south); `_pXsZs` (SummaGEMM: X_addr west -> south, Z_eaddr west -> south); `_pZs` (SummaGEMM: Z_eaddr west -> south); `_pCwIsOsSw` (RoPE: C_addr south -> west, I_addr west -> south, O_eaddr west -> south, S_addr south -> west). |
| `addi` | residual add as upstream's plan runs it: the Activation kernel with function 'none' and a full-size bias (the residual stream). |
| (fixed) / (fallback) | plan runs: upstream's setting with a recorded fix (it failed the output check or could not run as given) / upstream's settings all failed, so the fastest passing earlier sweep setting is used. |
| f_pad · f_occ · f_rest | MFU factors of a matrix kernel: true / padded FLOP (shape padding x RedMulE block fill) · active clusters / 64 · the matrix units' busy share inside the active clusters (everything else: data movement, sync, overhead). |
| roofline bound / × roofline | which lower limit is larger, true FLOP at 131.1 TFLOP/s or the operator's unique bytes at 1,024 GB/s, and how many times that limit the measured time is. A large × roofline means latency, sync or overhead dominate, whatever the bound says. |
| MFU | all FLOP of the stage or call (row-operator FLOP included) at the 131.1 TFLOP/s RedMulE peak / time. One definition on every tile and table of this page. |

| prefix | expert | K and V of 16 prefix layers, 241 x 320 each (cross layers project them once per call; self layers attend over 241 + 50 rows) | 4.936 | once per call, read every step |
| expert | output | action chunk 50 x 32, Euler-updated each step | 0.003 | 10 steps |

## Assumptions behind every number

* fp16 operands (the kernels' precision); weight footprint = parameters x 2 B.
* Every kernel runs alone on all 64 clusters; kernels run one after another, so times add (no overlap between kernels or stages).
* Every kernel reads its inputs from HBM and writes its output to HBM: no on-chip reuse between kernels.
* HBM: DRAMSys, 1,024 GB/s peak (measured: 16 channels x 64 GB/s).
* Attention is unmasked (stage1-spec §4.2): dense FLOP and time, no causal or padding savings.
* Expert self-attention's KV concatenation is not modelled (as upstream's plan).
* Host-side, not timed: `lang_embed_scale` (prefix), `state_proj` (prefix), `bias_state` (prefix).
* Plan runs and plan-constrained sweep runs are not traced (no per-cluster busy data).
* Every time on these pages comes from a run under the deployment plan: inputs and outputs in the layout and HBM edge the neighbouring kernels use (GEMM reshape on store / load, padded GEMM rows, placement overrides). The earlier sweep preset (`constants.yaml h1_kernels`: each kernel with its inputs preloaded as it wants them, so splitting, head-major conversion, padding and placement were free) is not a deployable plan and is not shown; it stays in constants.yaml for the cost-model fit.

## What this baseline cannot tell you

For studies that split or recombine the vision encoder, prefix and action expert:

* Stage time on part of the mesh: every run used the full mesh, so there is no data on how a stage scales on fewer clusters (needed to place the vision encoder, prefix and expert side by side).
* Concurrency: no runs of two stages at once, so no HBM or NoC contention data.
* Overlap and pipelining between kernels or stages (all times here add serially).
* Gains from fusion or on-chip reuse: every kernel round-trips HBM.
* Masked attention and KV concatenation costs.

## Where the time goes (estimate)

Each matrix kernel's time split as: ideal (true FLOP at the 131.1 TFLOP/s peak) + padding (padded FLOP, same rate: shape padding to whole tiles, and for GEMM RedMulE array padding to whole 32 x 64 output blocks, see below) + idle clusters (padded FLOP on only the active clusters) + HBM floor (the extra time if the operator's unique bytes, each moved once, need longer at 1,024 GB/s than the compute above; that bandwidth is DRAMSys's peak, 16 channels x 64 GB/s) + rest (time beyond that roofline: tiling re-reads, NoC, synchronisation, per-call overhead, HBM below peak). Row operators (vector cores) are counted whole. MFU = all FLOP at peak / time, as on the whole page (row-operator FLOP included, a small share). Times in ms per call.

## Matrix kernels

MFU = f_pad x f_occ x f_rest. f_pad = true / padded FLOP = shape padding x RedMulE block fill (below); f_occ = active clusters / 64; f_rest = the rest, the matrix units' share of time inside the active clusters. Roofline bound: which of the two lower limits, true FLOP at peak or the operator's unique bytes at 1,024 GB/s, is larger; x roofline = measured time / that limit (a large value means latency, sync or overhead dominate, whatever the bound). Time in µs per call; call totals are on the operator-graph pages.

### f_pad in words

f_pad = shape padding x RedMulE block fill. Shape padding: the operator rounded up to whole tiles. Block fill: how much of the area RedMulE times holds the tile, since it times each call in whole 32 x 64 output blocks (a 128 x 96 tile runs as 128 x 128, block fill 0.75).

### Why RedMulE block fill counts in f_pad

GVSoC's RedMulE model times every call in output blocks of 32 rows x 64 columns (redmule_h x redmule_w * (redmule_pipe + 1) from constants.yaml arch.h1), at redmule_pipe + 1 = 2 cycles per reduction element per block, however many of the block's columns hold data (`light_redmule.cpp`, `init_redmule_meta_data` and `get_redmule_array_runtime`). On H1 a tile of 128 x 96 thus takes the time of 128 x 128: 75 % of the array time does real MACs (block fill 0.75). This is counted with shape padding in f_pad, not left in f_rest, because:

* it is the same kind of loss: array time spent on work that is not in the operator (empty block slots instead of zero rows), at the full peak rate;
* the mapping fixes it before the kernel runs: it follows from the tile shape and the arch alone, so it can be computed for every candidate, traced or not, and a different tile or mapping removes it;
* f_rest then keeps only the run-time losses (data movement, synchronisation, per-call overhead, pipeline fill), which need traces or a cost model to explain.

The per-call rule ceil(m/32) x ceil(n/64) x k x 2 cycles + about 160 cycles matched the RedMulE busy time per call of the traced GEMM runs (estimate; fit in cost-model-h1.md section 3). Array padding is modelled for GEMM only: FlatAttention's RedMulE call shapes have not been read yet, so attention keeps block fill = 1. The interpretation that each CE interleaves ce_pipe + 1 outputs to hide the FMA latency is an inference; the timing rule itself is the simulator's code.

## Mapping space per GEMM shape

Valid settings per technique (the driver's candidate generator: tiles multiples of 32 up to 256, L1 double buffers within 352 KiB, padded work at most 2.5x) / runs in the sweeps (passing the output check). A dash: the technique was not enumerated for this shape. Sweep-preset shapes only; W1's plan runs per key are in the plan section above.

| shape | Nosplit | splitN, square groups | splitN, non-square groups | splitK, square groups | splitK, non-square groups | selected |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |

In the kernel but never swept (per shape in the explorer): splitK beyond upstream's setting on M > 64 shapes (only upstream opt()'s own splitK setting ran (gemm_upstream.py); no tile or group sweep. splitK is correct only with all 64 clusters busy and at most 2 N steps per group (wrong-output-runs-h1.md)); non-square groups with M_iter > 1 (not runnable: SummaGEMM.h:165 steps X along M by summa_group_x); reshape on load / store (resha_x_from, resha_z_to; TALL / THIN) (in the kernel config, never enabled). Row kernels: Activation's bias_enable (bias added in the same pass) is never run; the bias before GELU is a separate Eltwise call.

The kernel code differs where the interface matches (our SummaGEMM store-range guard, FlatAttention `sqrt_dim`, Activation fixes and GELU). Kernel directories only upstream has (`Other`: microbenchmarks), not run here: `FA`, `FlatMLA`, `MoECombine`, `MoEDispatch`, `MoEGate`, `Other` (`RoPE` is relevant: rope runs here as an Eltwise op).

* **pick**: per run key (upstream deployment plan, `h1_plan` / `h1_plan_w1b`): the selected run is the fastest with a passing output check among the plan runs of its key (upstream's candidates and the recorded fixes, `results/plan_runs_h1.csv`), and its time is the one in `constants.yaml`.
* **own runs**: every pick of the plan-constrained sweep is a run of its own (`results/plan_sweep_h1.csv`) that passed the output check, for the key and run variant (padded sizes) the pick names, with the time `constants.yaml` holds. The two plans share no runs.
* **reproducible**: a run both drivers made (upstream's run variant and setting, in `plan_runs_h1.csv` and `plan_sweep_h1.csv`) has the same status and the same time: a check on the simulator and the drivers, not a comparison of plans; it catches drift between the two drivers (flags, placement overrides). Plans are independent and may be better or worse than one another, so no check compares their times.
* **placement**: for every traced setting, the clusters the kernel's group placement makes active (`placement()`, from `flex_group_barrier.h:43` and `SummaGEMM.h:131-138`) are exactly the clusters with RedMulE activity in the kernel window of the trace (`results/trace_summary_h1.json`). Coverage: the traces are of square groups (1x1, 2x2) and attention only. The selected non-square and splitK expert mappings and the scale-8 picks have no trace, so their mesh diagrams rest on the kernel source alone.
* **sum**: count x kernel time over all operators gives the composed time of the operator-graph page; the expert's per-step and once-per-call rows add up to the expert stage.
